docs.text: FastAPI In this notebook we build a small travel-booking REST API with FastAPI, one feature at a time. We start with a single file that returns hard-coded JSON and finish with a database, routers, middleware, API keys and JWT login. Learning Objectives By the end of this notebook you will be able to: Build a REST API with FastAPI and run it with uvicorn Read path parameters, query parameters and JSON request bodies Validate input and shape output with Pydantic request/response models Store data in SQLite with SQLAlchemy and FastAPI's Depends() Split a growing app into separate files with APIRouter Add logging and CORS middleware Protect routes with an API key Add username/password login that issues JWT access tokens with an expiry time Prerequisites Python 3.10 or newer The OOP notebook (classes, type hints) and basic SQL Some idea of what HTTP methods (GET, POST, ...) and status codes (200, 404, ...) are Install everything used in this notebook: pip install "fastapi[standard]" sqlalchemy pyjwt bcrypt fastapi[standard] also installs uvicorn (the server), httpx (used by TestClient ) and python-multipart (needed for the login form in Section 8). How to Use This Notebook Work through it top to bottom . Each section adds one feature to the same project, called travelapi . Most code cells are files , not cells to run here. A cell that starts with # file: travelapi/app/main.py is the full content of that file: create (or replace) the file and paste it in. Cells marked Illustration are short pieces to read, not to copy. Sections 1 to 3 also have small cells marked Runs in the notebook . They use FastAPI's TestClient to call the API without starting a server, so you can try things right here. From Section 4 on, run the real server from inside the travelapi/ folder with uvicorn app.main:app --reload and test in the browser at http://localhost:8000/docs . Try each Exercise yourself before opening Show solution . Each section ends with a Quick recap . Read just the recaps when revising. What We're Building We will build the Travel API : a REST API for browsing destinations, booking trips and managing users. Client (curl / browser / Swagger UI) | | HTTP v [ FastAPI + uvicorn ] <-- your Python code | | SQL v [ SQLite ] <-- travel.db Final Endpoint Table Method Path Auth Description GET /destinations None List all destinations GET /destinations/{id} None Get one destination POST /destinations API Key Create a destination DELETE /destinations/{id} API Key Delete a destination GET /trips None List all trips GET /trips/{id} None Get one trip POST /trips API Key Create a trip POST /auth/register None Register a user POST /auth/token None Get a JWT token POST /bookings JWT Create a booking GET /bookings/me JWT My bookings PATCH /bookings/{id}/cancel JWT Cancel a booking Project Structure This is where we'll end up. Don't create it all now; each section tells you which file to add. travelapi/ ├── app/ │ ├── __init__.py (empty) │ ├── main.py │ ├── database.py │ ├── dependencies/ │ │ ├── __init__.py (empty) │ │ ├── auth.py (API key) │ │ └── jwt_auth.py (JWT) │ └── routers/ │ ├── __init__.py (empty) │ ├── destinations.py │ ├── trips.py │ ├── bookings.py │ └── auth.py └── requirements.txt Quick recap We're building one project, travelapi , and growing it section by section. Public routes let anyone read. Writing destinations and trips needs an API key; bookings need a JWT login. Data lives in a SQLite file, travel.db , from Section 4 onwards. 1. First Routes What Is FastAPI? FastAPI is a modern Python web framework for building REST APIs. What makes it pleasant to use: Type hints drive everything. Route parameters, request bodies and response shapes are all declared with ordinary Python types. Validation is automatic. Pydantic checks every incoming request. Bad data gets a 422 response with a clear message, and your function never runs. Docs for free. Swagger UI at /docs and ReDoc at /redoc , with no extra code. It's fast. It's built on Starlette and runs on uvicorn, and is one of the fastest Python frameworks around. Project Setup Create the project folder: mkdir -p travelapi/app cd travelapi touch app/__init__.py Create travelapi/requirements.txt : fastapi[standard]>=0.115 sqlalchemy>=2.0 pyjwt>=2.8 bcrypt>=4.1 Paste the code cell below into app/main.py , then start the server from the travelapi/ folder: uvicorn app.main:app --reload app.main:app means "in the module app/main.py , use the variable app ". --reload restarts the server every time you save a file. Now visit: http://localhost:8000/ for the raw JSON response http://localhost:8000/docs for Swagger UI, where you can try every endpoint http://localhost:8000/redoc for the ReDoc version of the docs How a Route Works @app.get("/destinations") <- HTTP method + URL path def list_destinations(): <- an ordinary Python function (sync or async) return [...] <- dict or list, FastAPI turns it into JSON The decorator connects a URL to a function. When a GET request arrives at /destinations , FastAPI calls list_destinations() and sends back whatever it returns as JSON. # file: travelapi/app/main.py (Section 1 checkpoint) from fastapi import FastAPI app = FastAPI ( title = "Travel API" , description = "A travel booking system" , version = "1.0.0" ) @app . get ( "/" ) def root (): return { "message" : "Welcome to the Travel API" } @app . get ( "/destinations" ) def list_destinations (): return [ { "id" : 1 , "name" : "Paris" , "country" : "France" , "price_per_day" : 150 }, { "id" : 2 , "name" : "Tokyo" , "country" : "Japan" , "price_per_day" : 120 }, { "id" : 3 , "name" : "Rome" , "country" : "Italy" , "price_per_day" : 100 }, ] @app . get ( "/trips" ) def list_trips (): return [ { "id" : 1 , "destination_id" : 1 , "start_date" : "2026-06-01" , "end_date" : "2026-06-07" , "spots_available" : 10 }, { "id" : 2 , "destination_id" : 2 , "start_date" : "2026-07-15" , "end_date" : "2026-07-22" , "spots_available" : 5 }, ] You can call this app without starting a server. TestClient sends fake HTTP requests straight to the app object, which is handy for quick checks and for writing tests later. Run the cell above first, then this one. # Runs in the notebook from fastapi.testclient import TestClient client = TestClient ( app ) response = client . get ( "/" ) print ( response . status_code , response . json ()) response = client . get ( "/destinations" ) print ( response . status_code , [ d [ "name" ] for d in response . json ()]) 200 {'message': 'Welcome to the Travel API'} 200 ['Paris', 'Tokyo', 'Rome'] Exercise 1: Add a Health Check Add a GET /health route that returns {"status": "ok", "version": "1.0.0"} . Check that it shows up in Swagger UI at /docs . Show solution # add to: travelapi/app/main.py @app . get ( "/health" ) def health (): return { "status" : "ok" , "version" : "1.0.0" } Quick recap app = FastAPI() creates the application; uvicorn app.main:app --reload serves it. @app.get("/path") connects a URL and HTTP method to a function. Return a dict or list and FastAPI sends it as JSON. Swagger UI at /docs is generated for you. Use it to try your endpoints. 2. Path & Query Parameters Path Parameters A path parameter is a variable that is part of the URL itself, like the 1 in /destinations/1 . Put {name} in the path and add a function argument with the same name: # Illustration (not a complete file) @app . get ( "/destinations/ {destination_id} " ) def get_destination ( destination_id : int ): ... FastAPI turns the text "1" from the URL into the Python int 1 for you. If the client sends "abc" , FastAPI returns 422 before your function is even called. Query Parameters A query parameter is anything after the ? in the URL: GET /destinations?country=France&max_price=200 . Declare them as function arguments with default values: def list_destinations ( country : str | None = None , max_price : float | None = None ): If country isn't in the URL, it's None . How does FastAPI know which is which? An argument whose name appears in the path string is a path parameter. Any other simple argument is a query parameter. Type Conversion URL value Python type hint Result "42" int 42 "3.14" float 3.14 "true" bool True (so do 1 , yes , on ) "abc" int 422 Unprocessable Entity Here is the whole file for this section. It keeps the data in a plain Python list for now. # file: travelapi/app/main.py (Section 2 checkpoint) from fastapi import FastAPI , HTTPException from typing import Optional app = FastAPI ( title = "Travel API" , version = "1.0.0" ) _destinations = [ { "id" : 1 , "name" : "Paris" , "country" : "France" , "price_per_day" : 150.0 }, { "id" : 2 , "name" : "Tokyo" , "country" : "Japan" , "price_per_day" : 120.0 }, { "id" : 3 , "name" : "Rome" , "country" : "Italy" , "price_per_day" : 100.0 }, ] @app . get ( "/destinations" ) def list_destinations ( country : Optional [ str ] = None , max_price : Optional [ float ] = None , ): result = _destinations if country : result = [ d for d in result if d [ "country" ] . lower () == country . lower ()] if max_price is not None : result = [ d for d in result if d [ "price_per_day" ] <= max_price ] return result @app . get ( "/destinations/ {destination_id} " ) def get_destination ( destination_id : int ): for dest in _destinations : if dest [ "id" ] == destination_id : return dest raise HTTPException ( status_code = 404 , detail = "Destination not found" ) @app . get ( "/trips" ) def list_trips ( destination_id : Optional [ int ] = None ): trips = [ { "id" : 1 , "destination_id" : 1 , "start_date" : "2026-06-01" , "end_date" : "2026-06-07" , "spots_available" : 10 }, { "id" : 2 , "destination_id" : 2 , "start_date" : "2026-07-15" , "end_date" : "2026-07-22" , "spots_available" : 5 }, ] if destination_id is not None : trips = [ t for t in trips if t [ "destination_id" ] == destination_id ] return trips Try a few URLs against it. Notice the 404 comes from our own HTTPException , while the 422 comes from FastAPI before our code runs. # Runs in the notebook from fastapi.testclient import TestClient client = TestClient ( app ) print ( client . get ( "/destinations" , params = { "country" : "france" }) . json ()) print ( client . get ( "/destinations" , params = { "max_price" : 120 }) . json ()) print ( client . get ( "/destinations/99" ) . status_code , client . get ( "/destinations/99" ) . json ()) print ( client . get ( "/destinations/abc" ) . status_code ) [{'id': 1, 'name': 'Paris', 'country': 'France', 'price_per_day': 150.0}] [{'id': 2, 'name': 'Tokyo', 'country': 'Japan', 'price_per_day': 120.0}, {'id': 3, 'name': 'Rome', 'country': 'Italy', 'price_per_day': 100.0}] 404 {'detail': 'Destination not found'} 422 Exercise 2: Minimum Price Filter Add an optional min_price query parameter to GET /destinations that removes destinations cheaper than the given value. Test it with /destinations?min_price=120 (you should get Paris and Tokyo). Show solution # add to: travelapi/app/main.py (replace list_destinations) @app . get ( "/destinations" ) def list_destinations ( country : Optional [ str ] = None , max_price : Optional [ float ] = None , min_price : Optional [ float ] = None , ): result = _destinations if country : result = [ d for d in result if d [ "country" ] . lower () == country . lower ()] if max_price is not None : result = [ d for d in result if d [ "price_per_day" ] <= max_price ] if min_price is not None : result = [ d for d in result if d [ "price_per_day" ] >= min_price ] return result Quick recap Path parameters: {name} in the path plus an argument with the same name. Query parameters: any other argument, usually with a default such as None . Type hints do the conversion. Bad values get a 422 automatically. Raise HTTPException(status_code=404, ...) when something isn't found. 3. Request & Response Models Why Two Models? FastAPI uses Pydantic models to describe the data going in and out: Request model ( DestinationCreate ): what the client sends. It can contain things you never want to send back, like a password. Response model ( DestinationResponse ): what the API returns. It can contain things the client never sends, like the id the server assigns. Keeping them separate means you can change one direction without affecting the other. response_model Passing response_model=DestinationResponse to the decorator tells FastAPI to: Validate your return value against the model Drop any fields that aren't in the model (so you can't leak data by accident) Show the response shape in Swagger UI Field Validation Field() from Pydantic adds rules directly on the model: Constraint Meaning min_length=1 String must not be empty max_length=100 String must not exceed 100 characters gt=0 Number must be greater than 0 ge=0 Number must be ≥ 0 le=500 Number must be ≤ 500 If a rule is broken, the client gets 422 Unprocessable Entity with a message saying which field failed. You don't write any validation code in the route. Testing Validation with curl # Missing required fields curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/destinations \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"name": "Berlin"}' # -> 422: country, description and price_per_day are required # price_per_day = 0 (breaks gt=0) curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/destinations \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"name": "Berlin", "country": "Germany", "description": "A vibrant European capital", "price_per_day": 0}' # -> 422: price_per_day must be greater than 0 # file: travelapi/app/main.py (Section 3 checkpoint) from fastapi import FastAPI , HTTPException from pydantic import BaseModel , Field from typing import Optional app = FastAPI ( title = "Travel API" , version = "1.0.0" ) class DestinationCreate ( BaseModel ): name : str = Field ( min_length = 1 , max_length = 100 ) country : str = Field ( min_length = 1 , max_length = 100 ) description : str = Field ( min_length = 10 ) price_per_day : float = Field ( gt = 0 ) class DestinationResponse ( BaseModel ): id : int name : str country : str description : str price_per_day : float class TripCreate ( BaseModel ): destination_id : int start_date : str = Field ( pattern = r "^\d {4} -\d {2} -\d {2} $" ) end_date : str = Field ( pattern = r "^\d {4} -\d {2} -\d {2} $" ) spots_available : int = Field ( gt = 0 ) class TripResponse ( BaseModel ): id : int destination_id : int start_date : str end_date : str spots_available : int _destinations : list [ dict ] = [] _trips : list [ dict ] = [] _dest_id = 1 _trip_id = 1 @app . get ( "/destinations" , response_model = list [ DestinationResponse ]) def list_destinations ( country : Optional [ str ] = None ): if country : return [ d for d in _destinations if d [ "country" ] . lower () == country . lower ()] return _destinations @app . get ( "/destinations/ {destination_id} " , response_model = DestinationResponse ) def get_destination ( destination_id : int ): for dest in _destinations : if dest [ "id" ] == destination_id : return dest raise HTTPException ( status_code = 404 , detail = "Destination not found" ) @app . post ( "/destinations" , response_model = DestinationResponse , status_code = 201 ) def create_destination ( destination : DestinationCreate ): global _dest_id record = { "id" : _dest_id , ** destination . model_dump ()} _destinations . append ( record ) _dest_id += 1 return record @app . get ( "/trips" , response_model = list [ TripResponse ]) def list_trips (): return _trips @app . post ( "/trips" , response_model = TripResponse , status_code = 201 ) def create_trip ( trip : TripCreate ): global _trip_id record = { "id" : _trip_id , ** trip . model_dump ()} _trips . append ( record ) _trip_id += 1 return record Here are the same two curl tests, plus a valid request, sent from the notebook: # Runs in the notebook from fastapi.testclient import TestClient client = TestClient ( app ) good = { "name" : "Berlin" , "country" : "Germany" , "description" : "A vibrant European capital" , "price_per_day" : 90 } r = client . post ( "/destinations" , json = good ) print ( r . status_code , r . json ()) r = client . post ( "/destinations" , json = { "name" : "Berlin" }) print ( r . status_code , [ err [ "loc" ][ - 1 ] for err in r . json ()[ "detail" ]]) r = client . post ( "/destinations" , json = { ** good , "price_per_day" : 0 }) print ( r . status_code , r . json ()[ "detail" ][ 0 ][ "msg" ]) 201 {'id': 1, 'name': 'Berlin', 'country': 'Germany', 'description': 'A vibrant European capital', 'price_per_day': 90.0} 422 ['country', 'description', 'price_per_day'] 422 Input should be greater than 0 What just happened? The first request passed validation, got an id and came back with 201 Created . The second listed every missing field. The third failed the gt=0 rule. In the last two cases create_destination never ran. Exercise 3: Tags Add a tags field (a list of strings, empty by default) to DestinationCreate and DestinationResponse . Each tag must be at most 20 characters. Check that ["beach", "culture"] is accepted and ["a" * 21] is rejected with 422 . Hint: Annotated[str, Field(max_length=20)] puts a rule on each item of the list. Show solution # add to: travelapi/app/main.py from typing import Annotated Tag = Annotated [ str , Field ( max_length = 20 )] class DestinationCreate ( BaseModel ): name : str = Field ( min_length = 1 , max_length = 100 ) country : str = Field ( min_length = 1 , max_length = 100 ) description : str = Field ( min_length = 10 ) price_per_day : float = Field ( gt = 0 ) tags : list [ Tag ] = [] class DestinationResponse ( BaseModel ): id : int name : str country : str description : str price_per_day : float tags : list [ str ] = [] # Note: `= []` is safe here. Pydantic copies the default for every # new object, unlike a plain function default argument. Quick recap Use one Pydantic model for input ( ...Create ) and another for output ( ...Response ). response_model= validates the output and hides fields that aren't declared. Field(min_length=..., gt=...) adds rules; breaking one gives a 422 . Use status_code=201 on routes that create something. 4. SQLAlchemy Integration Why Move to a Database? The lists from Section 3 are emptied every time the server restarts. SQLAlchemy maps Python classes to database tables, and FastAPI's dependency system hands each request its own database session. How Depends(get_db) Works # Illustration (the real version is in database.py below) def get_db (): db = SessionLocal () try : yield db # ← session handed to the route function finally : db . close () # ← always runs after the response is sent @app . get ( "/destinations" ) def list_destinations ( db : Session = Depends ( get_db )): ... For every request, FastAPI calls get_db() , passes the session in as db , and runs the finally block (closing the session) after the response is sent. Your route never has to open or close a session itself. Files for This Section travelapi/app/ ├── __init__.py (empty, from Section 1) ├── database.py <- engine, session factory, ORM models, get_db └── main.py <- FastAPI app and routes Paste the first cell below into app/database.py and the second into app/main.py (replacing the old version). The server reloads by itself; if it isn't running, start it from the travelapi/ folder: uvicorn app.main:app --reload The imports say from app.database import ... , so always run uvicorn from the Routers The Problem With One Big main.py As the API grows, one main.py with every route in it gets hard to find your way around. APIRouter lets you put related routes in their own file, each with its own URL prefix and Swagger tag, and plug them all into main.py . How APIRouter Works # Illustration: routers/destinations.py from fastapi import APIRouter router = APIRouter ( prefix = "/destinations" , tags = [ "Destinations" ]) @router . get ( "" ) # matches GET /destinations def list_destinations (): ... @router . get ( "/ {id} " ) # matches GET /destinations/{id} def get_destination ( id : int ): ... # Illustration: main.py from app.routers import destinations app . include_router ( destinations . router ) APIRouter parameter Effect prefix="/destinations" Adds /destinations in front of every route in this router tags=["Destinations"] Groups these routes under one heading in Swagger UI Why "" and not "/" ? With a prefix, @router.get("/") would create the URL /destinations/ (with a trailing slash). A request to /destinations then gets a 307 redirect. Browsers follow that silently, but curl -X POST does not, so your POST would seem to do nothing. Using "" keeps the URLs exactly as in the endpoint table. Middleware is code that runs before every request reaches a route and after every response leaves it. It wraps the whole request/response cycle. Request -> [Middleware 1] -> [Middleware 2] -> Route Function Response <- [Middleware 1] <- [Middleware 2] <- Route Function Common uses: logging, CORS, authentication checks, rate limiting, adding response headers. BaseHTTPMiddleware # Illustration (imports left out) from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware class LoggingMiddleware ( BaseHTTPMiddleware ): async def dispatch ( self , request : Request , call_next ): # Code here runs BEFORE the route response = await call_next ( request ) # Code here runs AFTER the route return response call_next(request) passes the request on to the next middleware (or the route) and gives you back its response. Anything before that line runs on the way in; anything after it runs on the way out. CORS Middleware Browsers block JavaScript fetch() calls to a different origin (for example from a React app on port 3000 to our API on port 8000) unless the server says it's allowed. FastAPI ships with CORSMiddleware for this: # Illustration (imports left out) app . add_middleware ( CORSMiddleware , allow_origins = [ "http://localhost:3000" ], # your frontend URL allow_methods = [ "*" ], allow_headers = [ "*" ], ) During development allow_origins=["*"] (any origin) is fine. In production, list the real frontend URLs instead. Middleware Order The middleware you add last becomes the outermost layer, so it sees the request first and the response last. In the file below LoggingMiddleware is added after CORSMiddleware , which means: it logs every request, including the OPTIONS "preflight" requests browsers send for CORS, and the time it measures includes the work done by the CORS layer. # file: travelapi/app/main.py (Section 6 checkpoint) import time from fastapi import FastAPI , Request from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware from app.database import create_tables from app.routers import destinations , trips , bookings class LoggingMiddleware ( BaseHTTPMiddleware ): async def dispatch ( self , request : Request , call_next ): start = time . time () response = await call_next ( request ) duration = time . time () - start print ( f " { request . method } { request . url . path } → { response . status_code } ( { duration : .3f } s)" ) response . headers [ "X-Process-Time" ] = f " { duration : .3f } " return response app = FastAPI ( title = "Travel API" , description = "A travel booking system" , version = "1.0.0" ) create_tables () app . add_middleware ( CORSMiddleware , allow_origins = [ "*" ], allow_methods = [ "*" ], allow_headers = [ "*" ], ) app . add_middleware ( LoggingMiddleware ) app . include_router ( destinations . router ) app . include_router ( trips . router ) app . include_router ( bookings . router ) @app . get ( "/" , tags = [ "Root" ]) def root (): return { "message" : "Welcome to the Travel API" } Exercise 6: Request IDs Extend LoggingMiddleware so every response also has an X-Request-ID header containing str(uuid.uuid4()) . An API key is a secret string the client sends in a request header. The server looks it up in its database before allowing the request. It's simple to build and works well for server-to-server calls. Client Server | | | POST /trips | | X-API-Key: abc123 ──────► | Look up abc123 in users table | | Found -> carry on | 201 Created ◄────── | APIKeyHeader # Illustration from fastapi.security import APIKeyHeader api_key_header = APIKeyHeader ( name = "X-API-Key" , auto_error = False ) auto_error=False means FastAPI won't reject a request with no header by itself. Our own dependency does that instead, so we choose the error message. Dependency Injection for Auth get_api_key (below) is a FastAPI dependency. JWT Authentication API Key vs JWT API Key JWT Storage Database lookup on every request Stateless: the server just checks the token's signature Expiry Lasts until someone revokes it Built-in exp (expiry) claim Contents Random string with no meaning Signed data (username, expiry, ...) Typical use Server-to-server, simple scripts Apps where people log in JWT Structure A JWT (JSON Web Token) is three base64url-encoded parts joined by dots: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9 <- header (which algorithm) .eyJzdWIiOiJhbHBoYSJ9 <- payload (claims: sub, exp, ...) .SflKxwRJSMeKKF2QT4fwpMeJf36P <- signature (HMAC-SHA256 of header + payload) The server signs the token with a secret key. Later it can check any token without touching the database: sign the header and payload again and compare with the signature. Anyone can read the payload, so never put secrets in it. OAuth2 Password Flow The client sends a username and password to POST /auth/token . The server checks them against the database. The server returns {"access_token": "<jwt>", "token_type": "bearer"} . The client sends the token on later requests in the header Authorization: Bearer <jwt> . The server decodes the token, reads the username and loads the User . Token Expiry The exp claim in the payload is a Unix timestamp. jwt.decode() checks it for us and raises ExpiredSignatureError once that time has passed. We catch that and return 401 Unauthorized with the message "Token has expired, please log in again" . Libraries We use two small libraries: PyJWT ( import jwt ) to create and check tokens bcrypt to hash passwords, so the database never stores the real password Older tutorials (and older versions of this notebook) use python-jose and passlib . passlib no longer works with current bcrypt releases, and the FastAPI docs have moved to PyJWT, so we follow them. The real password is never stored. create_access_token adds an exp time to the data and signs it. get_current_user is a dependency, just like get_api_key . OAuth2PasswordBearer pulls the token out of the Authorization: Bearer ... header. Then we decode it, catching the expired case before the general invalid-token case, because ExpiredSignatureError is a kind of InvalidTokenError . # file: travelapi/app/routers/auth.py import secrets from fastapi import APIRouter , HTTPException , Depends from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordRequestForm from pydantic import BaseModel , Field from sqlalchemy.orm import Session from app.database import User , get_db from app.dependencies.jwt_auth import hash_password , verify_password , create_access_token router = APIRouter ( prefix = "/auth" , tags = [ "Authentication" ]) class UserCreate ( BaseModel ): username : str = Field ( min_length = 3 , max_length = 50 ) password : str = Field ( min_length = 8 ) class UserResponse ( BaseModel ): id : int username : str api_key : str model_config = { "from_attributes" : True } class Token ( BaseModel ): access_token : str token_type : str @router . post ( "/register" , response_model = UserResponse , status_code = 201 ) def register ( user : UserCreate , db : Session = Depends ( get_db )): if db . query ( User ) . filter ( User . username == user . username ) . first (): raise HTTPException ( status_code = 400 , detail = "Username already taken" ) db_user = User ( username = user . username , hashed_password = hash_password ( user . password ), api_key = secrets . token_urlsafe ( 32 ), ) db . add ( db_user ) db . commit () db . refresh ( db_user ) return db_user @router . post ( "/token" , response_model = Token ) def login ( form_data : OAuth2PasswordRequestForm = Depends (), db : Session = Depends ( get_db )): user = db . query ( User ) . filter ( User . username == form_data . username ) . first () if not user or not verify_password ( form_data . password , user . hashed_password ): raise HTTPException ( status_code = 401 , detail = "Incorrect username or password" , headers = { "WWW-Authenticate" : "Bearer" }, ) token = create_access_token ( data = { "sub" : user . username }) return { "access_token" : token , "token_type" : "bearer" } OAuth2PasswordRequestForm reads the username and password from a form (not JSON), because that's what the OAuth2 standard says. That's why the curl call below uses -d 'username=...&password=...' , and why python-multipart has to be installed. It also makes the Authorize button in Swagger UI work. # file: travelapi/app/main.py (Section 8 checkpoint: final main.py) import time from fastapi import FastAPI , Request from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware from app.database import create_tables from app.routers import destinations , trips , bookings , auth as auth_router class LoggingMiddleware ( BaseHTTPMiddleware ): async def dispatch ( self , request : Request , call_next ): start = time . time () response = await call_next ( request ) duration = time . time () - start print ( f " { request . method } { request . url . path } → { response . status_code } ( { duration : .3f } s)" ) response . headers [ "X-Process-Time" ] = f " { duration : .3f } " return response app = FastAPI ( title = "Travel API" , description = "A travel booking system" , version = "1.0.0" ) create_tables () app . add_middleware ( CORSMiddleware , allow_origins = [ "*" ], allow_methods = [ "*" ], allow_headers = [ "*" ], ) app . add_middleware ( LoggingMiddleware ) app . include_router ( auth_router . router ) app . include_router ( destinations . router ) app . include_router ( trips . router ) app . include_router ( bookings . router ) @app . get ( "/" , tags = [ "Root" ]) def root (): return { "message" : "Welcome to the Travel API" } Testing the Flow # 1. Register curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/register \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"username": "alice", "password": "secret123"}' # 2. Get a token curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/token \ -d 'username=alice&password=secret123' # -> {"access_token": "eyJ...", "token_type": "bearer"} # 3. Use the token (paste your access_token value) curl http://localhost:8000/bookings/me \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer eyJ...' Step 3 only checks the token once Section 9 is done. Until then /bookings/me doesn't exist yet. Exercise 8: Watch a Token Expire Make a token that is already expired and confirm that a protected endpoint returns 401 with "Token has expired, please log in again" . The slow way: set ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES = 1 , get a token, wait 70 seconds, call a protected endpoint, then set it back to 30 . The quick way is in the solution. Show solution # Run from the travelapi/ folder (python, or a test file). # Do Section 9 first so /bookings/me exists and checks the token. from datetime import timedelta from fastapi.testclient import TestClient from app.main import app from app.dependencies.jwt_auth import create_access_token client = TestClient ( app ) client . post ( "/auth/register" , json = { "username" : "alice" , "password" : "secret123" }) expired = create_access_token ({ "sub" : "alice" }, expires_delta = timedelta ( seconds =- 1 )) r = client . get ( "/bookings/me" , headers = { "Authorization" : f "Bearer { expired } " }) print ( r . status_code , r . json ()) # 401 {'detail': 'Token has expired, please log in again'} Quick recap Passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes, never as plain text. POST /auth/token checks the password and returns a signed JWT with an exp time. Clients send Authorization: Bearer <token> ; Depends(get_current_user) checks it and loads the user. Catch ExpiredSignatureError before InvalidTokenError if you want a separate "expired" message. 9. Final Challenge: Bookings Build the complete Bookings feature by replacing the stub routers/bookings.py with a full version. Requirements POST /bookings (JWT-protected) creates a booking for the logged-in user. Return 404 if the trip doesn't exist. Return 400 if spots_available <= 0 . Decrease the trip's spots_available by 1. Return the booking with status "confirmed" . GET /bookings/me (JWT-protected) returns all bookings of the logged-in user. PATCH /bookings/{id}/cancel (JWT-protected) cancels one of the user's bookings. Return 404 if the booking doesn't exist or belongs to someone else . Return 400 if it's already cancelled. Give the spot back: increase spots_available by 1. Check It With Swagger UI Start the server and open http://localhost:8000/docs . Register a user with POST /auth/register . Copy the api_key from the response. Click Authorize and log in with the same username and password. Swagger calls /auth/token and remembers the token for you. Create a destination and a trip. Use the API key from step 1 in the X-API-Key field. Create a booking and check that the trip's spots_available went down by 1. Cancel the booking and check that spots_available went back up. Cancel the same booking again and check you get 400 Bad Request . Show solution # file: travelapi/app/routers/bookings.py (Section 9 solution) from fastapi import APIRouter , HTTPException , Depends from pydantic import BaseModel from sqlalchemy.orm import Session from app.database import Booking , Trip , User , get_db from app.dependencies.jwt_auth import get_current_user router = APIRouter ( prefix = "/bookings" , tags = [ "Bookings" ]) class BookingCreate ( BaseModel ): trip_id : int class BookingResponse ( BaseModel ): id : int trip_id : int user_id : int status : str model_config = { "from_attributes" : True } @router . post ( "" , response_model = BookingResponse , status_code = 201 ) def create_booking ( booking : BookingCreate , db : Session = Depends ( get_db ), current_user : User = Depends ( get_current_user ), ): trip = db . query ( Trip ) . filter ( Trip . id == booking . trip_id ) . first () if not trip : raise HTTPException ( status_code = 404 , detail = "Trip not found" ) if trip . spots_available <= 0 : raise HTTPException ( status_code = 400 , detail = "No spots available for this trip" ) db_booking = Booking ( trip_id = booking . trip_id , user_id = current_user . id , status = "confirmed" ) trip . spots_available -= 1 db . add ( db_booking ) db . commit () db . refresh ( db_booking ) return db_booking @router . get ( "/me" , response_model = list [ BookingResponse ]) def my_bookings ( db : Session = Depends ( get_db ), current_user : User = Depends ( get_current_user ), ): return db . query ( Booking ) . filter ( Booking . user_id == current_user . id ) . all () @router . patch ( "/ {booking_id} /cancel" , response_model = BookingResponse ) def cancel_booking ( booking_id : int , db : Session = Depends ( get_db ), current_user : User = Depends ( get_current_user ), ): booking = db . query ( Booking ) . filter ( Booking . id == booking_id , Booking . user_id == current_user . id , ) . first () if not booking : raise HTTPException ( status_code = 404 , detail = "Booking not found" ) if booking . status == "cancelled" : raise HTTPException ( status_code = 400 , detail = "Booking is already cancelled" ) booking . status = "cancelled" trip = db . query ( Trip ) . filter ( Trip . id == booking . trip_id ) . first () if trip : trip . spots_available += 1 db . commit () db . refresh ( booking ) return booking Notice the cancel query filters on both Booking.id and Booking.user_id . That one line is what stops Bob from cancelling Alice's booking just by guessing its id. We answer 404 rather than 403 so we don't even reveal that the booking exists. Quick recap A route can use several dependencies at once: Depends(get_db) and Depends(get_current_user) . Always filter by the current user when reading or changing "my" data. Change related rows (the trip's spots) in the same commit() as the booking. Extra Practice A few more small features to try on the finished project. Each one only touches one file. Practice 1: Update a Destination with PATCH Add PATCH /destinations/{destination_id} (API-key protected). The client may send any of the fields; only the ones sent should change. Return 404 if the destination doesn't exist. Hint: make a DestinationUpdate model where every field is optional, and use model_dump(exclude_unset=True) to get only the fields the client actually sent. Show solution # add to: travelapi/app/routers/destinations.py from typing import Optional class DestinationUpdate ( BaseModel ): name : Optional [ str ] = Field ( default = None , min_length = 1 , max_length = 100 ) country : Optional [ str ] = Field ( default = None , min_length = 1 , max_length = 100 ) description : Optional [ str ] = Field ( default = None , min_length = 10 ) price_per_day : Optional [ float ] = Field ( default = None , gt = 0 ) @router . patch ( "/ {destination_id} " , response_model = DestinationResponse ) def update_destination ( destination_id : int , changes : DestinationUpdate , db : Session = Depends ( get_db ), current_user : User = Depends ( get_api_key ), ): dest = db . query ( Destination ) . filter ( Destination . id == destination_id ) . first () if not dest : raise HTTPException ( status_code = 404 , detail = "Destination not found" ) for field , value in changes . model_dump ( exclude_unset = True ) . items (): setattr ( dest , field , value ) db . commit () db . refresh ( dest ) return dest Practice 2: Filter Trips Let GET /trips take two optional query parameters: destination_id (only trips to that destination) and min_spots (only trips with at least that many free spots). For example /trips?destination_id=1&min_spots=5 . Show solution # add to: travelapi/app/routers/trips.py (replace list_trips) from typing import Optional @router . get ( "" , response_model = list [ TripResponse ]) def list_trips ( destination_id : Optional [ int ] = None , min_spots : Optional [ int ] = None , db : Session = Depends ( get_db ), ): query = db . query ( Trip ) if destination_id is not None : query = query . filter ( Trip . destination_id == destination_id ) if min_spots is not None : query = query . filter ( Trip . spots_available >= min_spots ) return query . all () Practice 3: Who Am I? Add GET /auth/me (JWT-protected) that returns the logged-in user's id and username . It must not return the password hash. Show solution # add to: travelapi/app/routers/auth.py from app.dependencies.jwt_auth import get_current_user class MeResponse ( BaseModel ): id : int username : str model_config = { "from_attributes" : True } @router . get ( "/me" , response_model = MeResponse ) def read_me ( current_user : User = Depends ( get_current_user )): return current_user # response_model drops hashed_password and api_key Quick recap PATCH = partial update: optional fields plus model_dump(exclude_unset=True) . Build a SQLAlchemy query step by step, adding .filter() only for the parameters that were sent. A response model is the easiest way to make sure secrets never leave the API. Summary & Cheat Sheet Topic Remember this First routes @app.get / @app.post + return a dict; FastAPI sends JSON. Run with uvicorn app.main:app --reload . Path & query params {id} in the path = path param; other arguments = query params. Type hints convert and validate. Pydantic models Separate ...Create (input) and ...Response (output) models. Field() adds rules; failures give 422 . SQLAlchemy + Depends get_db() yields a session per request and closes it afterwards. add , commit , refresh . Routers APIRouter(prefix=..., tags=...) per file; app.include_router() in main.py . Middleware BaseHTTPMiddleware.dispatch wraps every request; CORSMiddleware for browser clients. API key auth APIKeyHeader + a dependency that looks the key up in the database. JWT auth OAuth2 password flow; bcrypt hashes passwords; PyJWT signs tokens with an exp time. Testing TestClient(app) calls your API without starting a server. Further Reading FastAPI documentation Pydantic documentation SQLAlchemy ORM tutorial PyJWT documentation OAuth2 explained What's Next The next notebook, Django , builds a similar REST API (a blog) with Django and Django REST Framework. Watch how much FastAPI made you write by hand that Django gives you out of the box, like the admin site, user accounts and migrations.

docs.text: In this notebook we build a small travel-booking REST API with FastAPI, one feature at a time. We start with a single file that returns hard-coded JSON and finish with a database, routers, middleware, API keys and JWT login.
docs.title: FastAPI

docs.text: By the end of this notebook you will be able to: Build a REST API with FastAPI and run it with uvicorn Read path parameters, query parameters and JSON request bodies Validate input and shape output with Pydantic request/response models Store data in SQLite with SQLAlchemy and FastAPI's Depends() Split a growing app into separate files with APIRouter Add logging and CORS middleware Protect routes with an API key Add username/password login that issues JWT access tokens with an expiry time
docs.title: Learning Objectives

docs.text: Python 3.10 or newer The OOP notebook (classes, type hints) and basic SQL Some idea of what HTTP methods (GET, POST, ...) and status codes (200, 404, ...) are Install everything used in this notebook: pip install "fastapi[standard]" sqlalchemy pyjwt bcrypt fastapi[standard] also installs uvicorn (the server), httpx (used by TestClient ) and python-multipart (needed for the login form in Section 8).

docs.text: Work through it top to bottom . Each section adds one feature to the same project, called travelapi . Most code cells are files , not cells to run here. A cell that starts with # file: travelapi/app/main.py is the full content of that file: create (or replace) the file and paste it in. Cells marked Illustration are short pieces to read, not to copy. Sections 1 to 3 also have small cells marked Runs in the notebook . They use FastAPI's TestClient to call the API without starting a server, so you can try things right here. From Section 4 on, run the real server from inside the travelapi/ folder with uvicorn app.main:app --reload and test in the browser at http://localhost:8000/docs . Try each Exercise yourself before opening Show solution . Each section ends with a Quick recap . Read just the recaps when revising.

docs.text: FastAPI is a modern Python web framework for building REST APIs. What makes it pleasant to use: Type hints drive everything. Route parameters, request bodies and response shapes are all declared with ordinary Python types. Validation is automatic. Pydantic checks every incoming request. Bad data gets a 422 response with a clear message, and your function never runs. Docs for free. Swagger UI at /docs and ReDoc at /redoc , with no extra code. It's fast. It's built on Starlette and runs on uvicorn, and is one of the fastest Python frameworks around.
docs.title: What Is FastAPI?

docs.text: Create the project folder: mkdir -p travelapi/app cd travelapi touch app/__init__.py Create travelapi/requirements.txt : fastapi[standard]>=0.115 sqlalchemy>=2.0 pyjwt>=2.8 bcrypt>=4.1 Paste the code cell below into app/main.py , then start the server from the travelapi/ folder: uvicorn app.main:app --reload app.main:app means "in the module app/main.py , use the variable app ". --reload restarts the server every time you save a file. Now visit: http://localhost:8000/ for the raw JSON response http://localhost:8000/docs for Swagger UI, where you can try every endpoint http://localhost:8000/redoc for the ReDoc version of the docs

docs.text: @app.get("/destinations") <- HTTP method + URL path def list_destinations(): <- an ordinary Python function (sync or async) return [...] <- dict or list, FastAPI turns it into JSON The decorator connects a URL to a function. When a GET request arrives at /destinations , FastAPI calls list_destinations() and sends back whatever it returns as JSON. # file: travelapi/app/main.py (Section 1 checkpoint) from fastapi import FastAPI app = FastAPI ( title = "Travel API" , description = "A travel booking system" , version = "1.0.0" ) @app . get ( "/" ) def root (): return { "message" : "Welcome to the Travel API" } @app . get ( "/destinations" ) def list_destinations (): return [ { "id" : 1 , "name" : "Paris" , "country" : "France" , "price_per_day" : 150 }, { "id" : 2 , "name" : "Tokyo" , "country" : "Japan" , "price_per_day" : 120 }, { "id" : 3 , "name" : "Rome" , "country" : "Italy" , "price_per_day" : 100 }, ] @app . get ( "/trips" ) def list_trips (): return [ { "id" : 1 , "destination_id" : 1 , "start_date" : "2026-06-01" , "end_date" : "2026-06-07" , "spots_available" : 10 }, { "id" : 2 , "destination_id" : 2 , "start_date" : "2026-07-15" , "end_date" : "2026-07-22" , "spots_available" : 5 }, ] You can call this app without starting a server. TestClient sends fake HTTP requests straight to the app object, which is handy for quick checks and for writing tests later. Run the cell above first, then this one. # Runs in the notebook from fastapi.testclient import TestClient client = TestClient ( app ) response = client . get ( "/" ) print ( response . status_code , response . json ()) response = client . get ( "/destinations" ) print ( response . status_code , [ d [ "name" ] for d in response . json ()]) 200 {'message': 'Welcome to the Travel API'} 200 ['Paris', 'Tokyo', 'Rome']
docs.title: How a Route Works

docs.text: Add a GET /health route that returns {"status": "ok", "version": "1.0.0"} . Check that it shows up in Swagger UI at /docs . Show solution # add to: travelapi/app/main.py @app . get ( "/health" ) def health (): return { "status" : "ok" , "version" : "1.0.0" } Quick recap app = FastAPI() creates the application; uvicorn app.main:app --reload serves it. @app.get("/path") connects a URL and HTTP method to a function. Return a dict or list and FastAPI sends it as JSON. Swagger UI at /docs is generated for you. Use it to try your endpoints.
docs.title: Exercise 1: Add a Health Check

docs.text: A path parameter is a variable that is part of the URL itself, like the 1 in /destinations/1 . Put {name} in the path and add a function argument with the same name: # Illustration (not a complete file) @app . get ( "/destinations/ {destination_id} " ) def get_destination ( destination_id : int ): ... FastAPI turns the text "1" from the URL into the Python int 1 for you. If the client sends "abc" , FastAPI returns 422 before your function is even called.
docs.title: Path Parameters

docs.text: A query parameter is anything after the ? in the URL: GET /destinations?country=France&max_price=200 . Declare them as function arguments with default values: def list_destinations ( country : str | None = None , max_price : float | None = None ): If country isn't in the URL, it's None . How does FastAPI know which is which? An argument whose name appears in the path string is a path parameter. Any other simple argument is a query parameter.
docs.title: Query Parameters

docs.text: URL value Python type hint Result "42" int 42 "3.14" float 3.14 "true" bool True (so do 1 , yes , on ) "abc" int 422 Unprocessable Entity Here is the whole file for this section. It keeps the data in a plain Python list for now. # file: travelapi/app/main.py (Section 2 checkpoint) from fastapi import FastAPI , HTTPException from typing import Optional app = FastAPI ( title = "Travel API" , version = "1.0.0" ) _destinations = [ { "id" : 1 , "name" : "Paris" , "country" : "France" , "price_per_day" : 150.0 }, { "id" : 2 , "name" : "Tokyo" , "country" : "Japan" , "price_per_day" : 120.0 }, { "id" : 3 , "name" : "Rome" , "country" : "Italy" , "price_per_day" : 100.0 }, ] @app . get ( "/destinations" ) def list_destinations ( country : Optional [ str ] = None , max_price : Optional [ float ] = None , ): result = _destinations if country : result = [ d for d in result if d [ "country" ] . lower () == country . lower ()] if max_price is not None : result = [ d for d in result if d [ "price_per_day" ] <= max_price ] return result @app . get ( "/destinations/ {destination_id} " ) def get_destination ( destination_id : int ): for dest in _destinations : if dest [ "id" ] == destination_id : return dest raise HTTPException ( status_code = 404 , detail = "Destination not found" ) @app . get ( "/trips" ) def list_trips ( destination_id : Optional [ int ] = None ): trips = [ { "id" : 1 , "destination_id" : 1 , "start_date" : "2026-06-01" , "end_date" : "2026-06-07" , "spots_available" : 10 }, { "id" : 2 , "destination_id" : 2 , "start_date" : "2026-07-15" , "end_date" : "2026-07-22" , "spots_available" : 5 }, ] if destination_id is not None : trips = [ t for t in trips if t [ "destination_id" ] == destination_id ] return trips Try a few URLs against it. Notice the 404 comes from our own HTTPException , while the 422 comes from FastAPI before our code runs. # Runs in the notebook from fastapi.testclient import TestClient client = TestClient ( app ) print ( client . get ( "/destinations" , params = { "country" : "france" }) . json ()) print ( client . get ( "/destinations" , params = { "max_price" : 120 }) . json ()) print ( client . get ( "/destinations/99" ) . status_code , client . get ( "/destinations/99" ) . json ()) print ( client . get ( "/destinations/abc" ) . status_code ) [{'id': 1, 'name': 'Paris', 'country': 'France', 'price_per_day': 150.0}] [{'id': 2, 'name': 'Tokyo', 'country': 'Japan', 'price_per_day': 120.0}, {'id': 3, 'name': 'Rome', 'country': 'Italy', 'price_per_day': 100.0}] 404 {'detail': 'Destination not found'} 422
docs.title: Type Conversion

docs.text: Add an optional min_price query parameter to GET /destinations that removes destinations cheaper than the given value. Test it with /destinations?min_price=120 (you should get Paris and Tokyo). Show solution # add to: travelapi/app/main.py (replace list_destinations) @app . get ( "/destinations" ) def list_destinations ( country : Optional [ str ] = None , max_price : Optional [ float ] = None , min_price : Optional [ float ] = None , ): result = _destinations if country : result = [ d for d in result if d [ "country" ] . lower () == country . lower ()] if max_price is not None : result = [ d for d in result if d [ "price_per_day" ] <= max_price ] if min_price is not None : result = [ d for d in result if d [ "price_per_day" ] >= min_price ] return result Quick recap Path parameters: {name} in the path plus an argument with the same name. Query parameters: any other argument, usually with a default such as None . Type hints do the conversion. Bad values get a 422 automatically. Raise HTTPException(status_code=404, ...) when something isn't found.

docs.text: FastAPI uses Pydantic models to describe the data going in and out: Request model ( DestinationCreate ): what the client sends. It can contain things you never want to send back, like a password. Response model ( DestinationResponse ): what the API returns. It can contain things the client never sends, like the id the server assigns. Keeping them separate means you can change one direction without affecting the other.
docs.title: Why Two Models?

docs.text: Passing response_model=DestinationResponse to the decorator tells FastAPI to: Validate your return value against the model Drop any fields that aren't in the model (so you can't leak data by accident) Show the response shape in Swagger UI
docs.title: response_model

docs.text: Field() from Pydantic adds rules directly on the model: Constraint Meaning min_length=1 String must not be empty max_length=100 String must not exceed 100 characters gt=0 Number must be greater than 0 ge=0 Number must be ≥ 0 le=500 Number must be ≤ 500 If a rule is broken, the client gets 422 Unprocessable Entity with a message saying which field failed. You don't write any validation code in the route.
docs.title: Field Validation

docs.text: # Missing required fields curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/destinations \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"name": "Berlin"}' # -> 422: country, description and price_per_day are required # price_per_day = 0 (breaks gt=0) curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/destinations \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"name": "Berlin", "country": "Germany", "description": "A vibrant European capital", "price_per_day": 0}' # -> 422: price_per_day must be greater than 0 # file: travelapi/app/main.py (Section 3 checkpoint) from fastapi import FastAPI , HTTPException from pydantic import BaseModel , Field from typing import Optional app = FastAPI ( title = "Travel API" , version = "1.0.0" ) class DestinationCreate ( BaseModel ): name : str = Field ( min_length = 1 , max_length = 100 ) country : str = Field ( min_length = 1 , max_length = 100 ) description : str = Field ( min_length = 10 ) price_per_day : float = Field ( gt = 0 ) class DestinationResponse ( BaseModel ): id : int name : str country : str description : str price_per_day : float class TripCreate ( BaseModel ): destination_id : int start_date : str = Field ( pattern = r "^\d {4} -\d {2} -\d {2} $" ) end_date : str = Field ( pattern = r "^\d {4} -\d {2} -\d {2} $" ) spots_available : int = Field ( gt = 0 ) class TripResponse ( BaseModel ): id : int destination_id : int start_date : str end_date : str spots_available : int _destinations : list [ dict ] = [] _trips : list [ dict ] = [] _dest_id = 1 _trip_id = 1 @app . get ( "/destinations" , response_model = list [ DestinationResponse ]) def list_destinations ( country : Optional [ str ] = None ): if country : return [ d for d in _destinations if d [ "country" ] . lower () == country . lower ()] return _destinations @app . get ( destination : DestinationCreate ): global _dest_id record = { "id" : _dest_id , ** destination . model_dump ()} _destinations . append ( record ) _dest_id += 1 return record @app . get ( "/trips" , Runs in the notebook from fastapi.testclient import TestClient client = TestClient ( app ) good = { "name" : "Berlin" , "country" : "Germany" , "description" : "A vibrant European capital" , "price_per_day" : 90 } r = client . post ( "/destinations" , json = good ) print ( r . status_code , r . json ()) r = client . post ( "/destinations" , json = { "name" : "Berlin" }) print ( r . status_code , [ err [ "loc" ][ - 1 ] for err in r . json ()[ "detail" ]]) r = client . post ( "/destinations" , json = { ** good , "price_per_day" : 0 }) print ( r . status_code , r . json ()[ "detail" ][ 0 ][ "msg" ]) 201 {'id': 1, 'name': 'Berlin', 'country': 'Germany', 'description': 'A vibrant European capital', 'price_per_day': 90.0} 422 ['country', 'description', 'price_per_day'] 422 The first request passed validation, got an id and came back with 201 Created . The second listed every missing field. The third failed the gt=0 rule. docs.text: Add a tags field (a list of strings, empty by default) to DestinationCreate and DestinationResponse . Each tag must be at most 20 characters. Check that ["beach", "culture"] is accepted and ["a" * 21] is rejected with 422 . Hint: Annotated[str, Field(max_length=20)] puts a rule on each item of the list. Show solution # add to: travelapi/app/main.py from typing import Annotated Tag = Annotated [ str , Field ( max_length = 20 )] class DestinationCreate ( BaseModel ): name : str = Field ( min_length = 1 , max_length = 100 ) country : str = Field ( min_length = 1 , max_length = 100 ) description : str = Field ( min_length = 10 ) price_per_day : float = Field ( gt = 0 ) tags : list [ Tag ] = [] class DestinationResponse ( BaseModel ): id : int name : str country : str description : str price_per_day : float tags : list [ str ] = [] # Note: `= []` is safe here. Pydantic copies the default for every # new object, unlike a plain function default argument. Quick recap Use one Pydantic model for input ( ...Create ) and another for output ( ...Response ). response_model= validates the output and hides fields that aren't declared. Field(min_length=..., gt=...) adds rules; breaking one gives a 422 . Use status_code=201 on routes that create something.

docs.text: The lists from Section 3 are emptied every time the server restarts. SQLAlchemy maps Python classes to database tables, and FastAPI's dependency system hands each request its own database session.
docs.title: Why Move to a Database?

docs.text: # Illustration (the real version is in database.py below) def get_db (): db = SessionLocal () try : yield db # ← session handed to the route function finally : db . close () # ← always runs after the response is sent @app . get ( "/destinations" ) def list_destinations ( db : Session = Depends ( get_db )): ... For every request, FastAPI calls get_db() , passes the session in as db , and runs the finally block (closing the session) after the response is sent. Your route never has to open or close a session itself.
docs.title: How Depends(get_db) Works

docs.text: travelapi/app/ ├── __init__.py (empty, from Section 1) ├── database.py <- engine, session factory, ORM models, get_db └── main.py <- FastAPI app and routes Paste the first cell below into app/database.py and the second into app/main.py (replacing the old version). The server reloads by itself; if it isn't running, start it from the travelapi/ folder: uvicorn app.main:app --reload The imports say from app.database import ... , so always run uvicorn from the travelapi/ folder, not from inside app/ . # file: travelapi/app/database.py import os from datetime import datetime , timezone from sqlalchemy import ( create_engine , Column , Integer , String , Float , DateTime , ForeignKey , ) from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base , sessionmaker , relationship DATABASE_URL = os . getenv ( "DATABASE_URL" , "sqlite:///./travel.db" ) engine = create_engine ( DATABASE_URL , connect_args = { "check_same_thread" : False }) SessionLocal = sessionmaker ( autocommit = False , autoflush = False , bind = engine ) Base = declarative_base () class Destination ( Base ): __tablename__ = "destinations" id = Column ( Integer , primary_key = True , index = True ) name = Column ( String , nullable = False ) country = Column ( String , nullable = False ) description = Column ( String , nullable = False ) price_per_day = Column ( Float , nullable = False ) trips = relationship ( "Trip" , back_populates = "destination" ) class Trip ( Base ): __tablename__ = "trips" id = Column ( Integer , primary_key = True , index = True ) destination_id = Column ( Integer , ForeignKey ( "destinations.id" ), nullable = False ) start_date = Column ( String , nullable = False ) end_date = Column ( String , nullable = False ) spots_available = Column ( Integer , nullable = False ) destination = relationship ( "Destination" , back_populates = "trips" ) bookings = relationship ( "Booking" , back_populates = "trip" ) class User ( Base ): __tablename__ = "users" id = Column ( Integer , primary_key = True , index = True ) username = Column ( String , unique = True , nullable = False ) hashed_password = Column ( String , nullable = False ) api_key = Column ( String , unique = True , nullable = True ) bookings = relationship ( "Booking" , back_populates = "user" ) class Booking ( Base ): __tablename__ = "bookings" id = Column ( Integer , primary_key = True , index = True ) trip_id = Column ( Integer , ForeignKey ( "trips.id" ), nullable = False ) user_id = Column ( Integer , ForeignKey ( "users.id" ), nullable = False ) status = Column ( String , default = "pending" ) created_at = Column ( DateTime , default = lambda : datetime . now ( timezone . utc )) trip = relationship ( "Trip" , back_populates = "bookings" ) user = relationship ( "User" , back_populates = "bookings" ) def get_db (): db = SessionLocal () try : yield db finally : db . close () def create_tables (): Base . metadata . create_all ( bind = engine ) Two small things in database.py : check_same_thread=False is a SQLite-only setting. FastAPI may use the session from a different thread than the one that created it, and SQLite would complain without it. created_at uses datetime.now(timezone.utc) . The older datetime.utcnow() is deprecated since Python 3.12. # file: travelapi/app/main.py (Section 4 checkpoint) from fastapi import FastAPI , HTTPException , Depends from pydantic import BaseModel , Field from sqlalchemy.orm import Session from app.database import Destination , Trip , get_db , create_tables app = FastAPI ( title = "Travel API" , version = "1.0.0" ) create_tables () class DestinationCreate ( BaseModel ): name : str = Field ( min_length = 1 , max_length = 100 ) country : str = Field ( min_length = 1 , max_length = 100 ) description : str = Field ( min_length = 10 ) price_per_day : float = Field ( gt = 0 ) class DestinationResponse ( BaseModel ): id : int name : str country : str description : str price_per_day : float model_config = { "from_attributes" : True } class TripCreate ( BaseModel ): destination_id : int start_date : str = Field ( pattern = r "^\d {4} -\d {2} -\d {2} $" ) end_date : str = Field ( pattern = r "^\d {4} -\d {2} -\d {2} $" ) spots_available : int = Field ( gt = 0 ) class TripResponse ( BaseModel ): id : int destination_id : int start_date : str end_date : str spots_available : int model_config = { "from_attributes" : True } @app . get ( "/destinations" , response_model = list [ DestinationResponse ]) def list_destinations ( db : Session = Depends ( get_db )): return db . query ( Destination ) . all () @app . get ( "/destinations/ {destination_id} " , response_model = DestinationResponse ) def get_destination ( destination_id : int , db : Session = Depends ( get_db )): dest = db . query ( Destination ) . filter ( Destination . id == destination_id ) . first () if not dest : raise HTTPException ( status_code = 404 , detail = "Destination not found" ) return dest @app . post ( "/destinations" , response_model = DestinationResponse , status_code = 201 ) def create_destination ( destination : DestinationCreate , db : Session = Depends ( get_db )): db_dest = Destination ( ** destination . model_dump ()) db . add ( db_dest ) db . commit () db . refresh ( db_dest ) return db_dest @app . delete ( "/destinations/ {destination_id} " , status_code = 204 ) def delete_destination ( destination_id : int , db : Session = Depends ( get_db )): dest = db . query ( Destination ) . filter ( Destination . id == destination_id ) . first () if not dest : raise HTTPException ( status_code = 404 , detail = "Destination not found" ) if dest . trips : raise HTTPException ( status_code = 409 , detail = "Delete this destination's trips first" ) db . delete ( dest ) db . commit () @app . get ( "/trips" , response_model = list [ TripResponse ]) def list_trips ( db : Session = Depends ( get_db )): return db . query ( Trip ) . all () @app . post ( "/trips" , response_model = TripResponse , status_code = 201 ) def create_trip ( trip : TripCreate , db : Session = Depends ( get_db )): db_trip = Trip ( ** trip . model_dump ()) db . add ( db_trip ) db . commit () db . refresh ( db_trip ) return db_trip What just happened? The routes look almost the same as before. The differences: Each route takes db: Session = Depends(get_db) and uses db.query(...) instead of a list. To save something: db.add(obj) , db.commit() , then db.refresh(obj) to load the id the database assigned. model_config = {"from_attributes": True} lets Pydantic read a SQLAlchemy object ( dest.name ) instead of only dicts ( dest["name"] ). delete_destination refuses ( 409 Conflict ) to delete a destination that still has trips. Without that check SQLAlchemy would try to set those trips' destination_id to NULL , the database would reject it, and the client would get a 500 error.

docs.text: main.py can fetch one destination but not one trip. Add GET /trips/{trip_id} that returns 404 if the trip doesn't exist. Test with a valid ID and with 999 . Show solution # add to: travelapi/app/main.py @app . get ( "/trips/ {trip_id} " , response_model = TripResponse ) def get_trip ( trip_id : int , db : Session = Depends ( get_db )): trip = db . query ( Trip ) . filter ( Trip . id == trip_id ) . first () if not trip : raise HTTPException ( status_code = 404 , detail = "Trip not found" ) return trip Quick recap database.py holds the engine, SessionLocal , the models and get_db() . db: Session = Depends(get_db) gives each request its own session, closed automatically. Create = add + commit + refresh . Read = db.query(Model).filter(...).first() or .all() . Add model_config = {"from_attributes": True} to response models that read ORM objects.

docs.text: As the API grows, one main.py with every route in it gets hard to find your way around. APIRouter lets you put related routes in their own file, each with its own URL prefix and Swagger tag, and plug them all into main.py .
docs.title: The Problem With One Big main.py

docs.text: # Illustration: routers/destinations.py from fastapi import APIRouter router = APIRouter ( prefix = "/destinations" , tags = [ "Destinations" ]) @router . get ( "" ) # matches GET /destinations def list_destinations (): ... @router . get ( "/ {id} " ) # matches GET /destinations/{id} def get_destination ( id : int ): ... # Illustration: main.py from app.routers import destinations app . include_router ( destinations . router ) APIRouter parameter Effect prefix="/destinations" Adds /destinations in front of every route in this router tags=["Destinations"] Groups these routes under one heading in Swagger UI Why "" and not "/" ? With a prefix, @router.get("/") would create the URL /destinations/ (with a trailing slash). A request to /destinations then gets a 307 redirect. Browsers follow that silently, but curl -X POST does not, so your POST would seem to do nothing. Using "" keeps the URLs exactly as in the endpoint table.

docs.text: Middleware is code that runs before every request reaches a route and after every response leaves it. It wraps the whole request/response cycle. Request -> [Middleware 1] -> [Middleware 2] -> Route Function Response <- [Middleware 1] <- [Middleware 2] <- Route Function Common uses: logging, CORS, authentication checks, rate limiting, adding response headers.
docs.title: What Is Middleware?

docs.text: # Illustration (imports left out) from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware class LoggingMiddleware ( BaseHTTPMiddleware ): async def dispatch ( self , request : Request , call_next ): # Code here runs BEFORE the route response = await call_next ( request ) # Code here runs AFTER the route return response call_next(request) passes the request on to the next middleware (or the route) and gives you back its response. Anything before that line runs on the way in; anything after it runs on the way out.
docs.title: BaseHTTPMiddleware

docs.text: Browsers block JavaScript fetch() calls to a different origin (for example from a React app on port 3000 to our API on port 8000) unless the server says it's allowed. FastAPI ships with CORSMiddleware for this: # Illustration (imports left out) app . add_middleware ( CORSMiddleware , allow_origins = [ "http://localhost:3000" ], # your frontend URL allow_methods = [ "*" ], allow_headers = [ "*" ], ) During development allow_origins=["*"] (any origin) is fine. In production, list the real frontend URLs instead.
docs.title: CORS Middleware

docs.text: The middleware you add last becomes the outermost layer, so it sees the request first and the response last. In the file below LoggingMiddleware is added after CORSMiddleware , which means: it logs every request, including the OPTIONS "preflight" requests browsers send for CORS, and the time it measures includes the work done by the CORS layer. # file: travelapi/app/main.py (Section 6 checkpoint) import time from fastapi import FastAPI , Request from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware from app.database import create_tables from app.routers import destinations , trips , bookings class LoggingMiddleware ( BaseHTTPMiddleware ): async def dispatch ( self , request : Request , call_next ): start = time . time () response = await call_next ( request ) duration = time . time () - start print ( f " { request . method } { request . url . path } → { response . status_code } ( { duration : .3f } s)" ) response . headers [ "X-Process-Time" ] = f " { duration : .3f } " return response app = FastAPI ( title = "Travel API" , description = "A travel booking system" , version = "1.0.0" ) create_tables () app . add_middleware ( CORSMiddleware , allow_origins = [ "*" ], allow_methods = [ "*" ], allow_headers = [ "*" ], ) app . add_middleware ( LoggingMiddleware ) app . include_router ( destinations . router ) app . include_router ( trips . router ) app . include_router ( bookings . router ) @app . get ( "/" , tags = [ "Root" ]) def root (): return { "message" : "Welcome to the Travel API" }
docs.title: Middleware Order

docs.text: Extend LoggingMiddleware so every response also has an X-Request-ID header containing str(uuid.uuid4()) . Check it with curl -i http://localhost:8000/destinations ( -i prints the response headers). Show solution # add to: travelapi/app/main.py (replace LoggingMiddleware) import uuid class LoggingMiddleware ( BaseHTTPMiddleware ): async def dispatch ( self , request : Request , call_next ): start = time . time () response = await call_next ( request ) duration = time . time () - start print ( f " { request . method } { request . url . path } → { response . status_code } ( { duration : .3f } s)" ) response . headers [ "X-Process-Time" ] = f " { duration : .3f } " response . headers [ "X-Request-ID" ] = str ( uuid . uuid4 ()) return response Quick recap Middleware wraps every request: code before await call_next(request) runs on the way in, code after runs on the way out. CORSMiddleware lets browser apps on other origins call your API. The last middleware added is the outermost one.
docs.title: Exercise 6: Request IDs

docs.text: An API key is a secret string the client sends in a request header. The server looks it up in its database before allowing the request. It's simple to build and works well for server-to-server calls. Client Server | | | POST /trips | | X-API-Key: abc123 ──────► | Look up abc123 in users table | | Found -> carry on | 201 Created ◄────── |
docs.title: What Is API Key Auth?

docs.text: # Illustration from fastapi.security import APIKeyHeader api_key_header = APIKeyHeader ( name = "X-API-Key" , auto_error = False ) auto_error=False means FastAPI won't reject a request with no header by itself. Our own dependency does that instead, so we choose the error message.
docs.title: APIKeyHeader

docs.text: get_api_key (below) is a FastAPI dependency. Add it to any route that needs protecting: @router . post ( "" , status_code = 201 ) def create_trip ( trip : TripCreate , db : Session = Depends ( get_db ), current_user : User = Depends ( get_api_key ), # <- protects the route ): If get_api_key raises an HTTPException , FastAPI sends that response straight away and the route function is never called.
docs.title: Dependency Injection for Auth

docs.text: Create an empty app/dependencies/__init__.py (so dependencies/ is a package), then add app/dependencies/auth.py from the first cell and replace app/routers/trips.py with the second. # file: travelapi/app/dependencies/auth.py from fastapi import Security , HTTPException , Depends from fastapi.security import APIKeyHeader from sqlalchemy.orm import Session from app.database import User , get_db api_key_header = APIKeyHeader ( name = "X-API-Key" , auto_error = False ) def get_api_key ( api_key : str = Security ( api_key_header ), db : Session = Depends ( get_db ), ) -> User : if not api_key : raise HTTPException ( status_code = 403 , detail = "API key required. Send it in the X-API-Key header" ) user = db . query ( User ) . filter ( User . api_key == api_key ) . first () if not user : raise HTTPException ( status_code = 403 , detail = "Invalid API key" ) return user # file: travelapi/app/routers/trips.py (Section 7: POST protected by API key) from fastapi import APIRouter , HTTPException , Depends from pydantic import BaseModel , Field from sqlalchemy.orm import Session from app.database import Trip , User , get_db from app.dependencies.auth import get_api_key router = APIRouter ( prefix = "/trips" , tags = [ "Trips" ]) class TripCreate ( BaseModel ): destination_id : int start_date : str = Field ( pattern = r "^\d {4} -\d {2} -\d {2} $" ) end_date : str = Field ( pattern = r "^\d {4} -\d {2} -\d {2} $" ) spots_available : int = Field ( gt = 0 ) class TripResponse ( BaseModel ): id : int destination_id : int start_date : str end_date : str spots_available : int model_config = { "from_attributes" : True } @router . get ( "" , response_model = list [ TripResponse ]) def list_trips ( db : Session = Depends ( get_db )): return db . query ( Trip ) . all () @router . get ( "/ {trip_id} " , response_model = TripResponse ) def get_trip ( trip_id : int , db : Session = Depends ( get_db )): trip = db . query ( Trip ) . filter ( Trip . id == trip_id ) . first () if not trip : raise HTTPException ( status_code = 404 , detail = "Trip not found" ) return trip @router . post ( "" , response_model = TripResponse , status_code = 201 ) def create_trip ( trip : TripCreate , db : Session = Depends ( get_db ), current_user : User = Depends ( get_api_key ), ): db_trip = Trip ( ** trip . model_dump ()) db . add ( db_trip ) db . commit () db . refresh ( db_trip ) return db_trip

10 ) price_per_day : float = Field ( gt = 0 ) class DestinationResponse ( BaseModel ): id : int name : str country : str description : str price_per_day : float model_config = { "from_attributes" : True } @router . get ( "" , response_model = list [ DestinationResponse ]) def list_destinations ( db : Session = Depends ( get_db )): return db . query ( Destination ) . all () @router . get ( "/ {destination_id} " , response_model = DestinationResponse ) def get_destination ( destination_id : int , db : Session = Depends ( get_db )): dest = db . query ( Destination ) . filter ( Destination . id == destination_id ) . first () if not dest : raise HTTPException ( status_code = 404 , detail = "Destination not found" ) return dest @router . post ( "" , response_model = DestinationResponse , status_code = 201 ) def create_destination ( destination : DestinationCreate , db : Session = Depends ( get_db ), current_user : User = Depends ( get_api_key ), ): db_dest = Destination ( ** destination . model_dump ()) db . add ( db_dest ) db . commit () db . refresh ( db_dest ) return db_dest @router . delete ( "/ {destination_id} " , status_code = 204 ) def delete_destination ( destination_id : int , db : Session = Depends ( get_db ), current_user : User = Depends ( get_api_key ), ): dest = db . query ( Destination ) . filter ( Destination . id == destination_id ) . first () if not dest : raise HTTPException ( status_code = 404 , detail = "Destination not found" ) if dest . trips : raise HTTPException ( status_code = 409 , detail = "Delete this destination's trips first" ) db . delete ( dest ) db . commit () Quick recap An API key is a secret sent in a header ( X-API-Key ) and checked against the database. Write the check once as a dependency, then add Depends(get_api_key) to each route that needs it. Raising HTTPException inside a dependency stops the request before the route runs.
